newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen, Hyundai in talks on LNG deal.
newsitem.headline: Yemen, Hyundai in talks on LNG deal.

text.p: Yemen is holding talks with South Korea's Hyundai and Japan's SODEC on the sale of part of its share in the Yemen Liquefied Natural Gas Co, an oil official said on Monday.
Last month Yemen signed a memorandum of understanding with Hyundai to sell it part of its 26 percent share in the gas firm.
"The negotiations aim at reaching a final agreement for the company's participation in the gas project," the official said of the talks now underway in Sanaa with a Hyundai delegation.
He said the Korean company's proposed stake was six percent.
The Middle East Economic Survey reported on Monday that Yemen intended eventually to sell 11 percent of its stake in the project, reducing its holding to 15 percent.
The official told Reuters another delegation from Japan's SODEC was in Sanaa for similar talks.
In January Yemen signed an agreement with a number of foreign firms for the $5 billion LNG project.

Under the deal France's Total SA would take a 36 percent stake in the project, U.S. Exxon Corp jointly with Hunt Oil 30 percent, South Korea's Yukong eight percent and the Yemeni government 26 percent.

First exports from the LNG project are slated for 2001 and will have to compete against rival LNG projects in Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi for gas markets. The company plans to produce an annual five million tonnes of LNG.
The official said Yemen was currently also holding talks with the state-run Korea Gas Co on the possible sale of its LNG to Kogas.
Yemen is a relatively small and independent oil producer.
